statement: Formal smoothness implies projective differentials, and retracts of formally smooth algebras are formally smooth
notes: The square-zero derivation lifting argument and the retract comparison are written in full.

statement: A separated local ring cannot have a projective module with a nonzero infinitely t-divisible element
notes: Embed a projective module into a free module and use coordinatewise t-adic separation.

statement: The formal exponential exp(t) is transcendental over K(t) in characteristic zero
notes: A minimal monic polynomial and its derivative force a nonzero rational function a to satisfy a prime equals d times a, which its pole order forbids.

statement: For characteristic-zero k contained in K and n positive, K[[t1,...,tn]] is never discretely formally smooth over k; its differentials are not projective
notes: No finite-dimensionality assumption on Omega K/k is needed. The nonzero infinitely divisible differential is d(exp(t1))−exp(t1)dt1.

statement: The positive-dimensional manuscript reading is proved; a reading including dimension zero is false
notes: Dimension zero is a separable characteristic-zero field extension and is formally smooth. The original scan was visually inspected; no priority claim.

statement: Infinite-dimensional coefficient differentials obstruct discrete formal smoothness of a positive-dimensional power series ring
notes: Fresh free-module coordinates and coefficientwise derivations prove the obstruction; independent agent audit passed.

statement: Infinite absolute p-rank still obstructs formal smoothness when the relative differential dimension is finite
notes: An infinite p-independent coefficient series has nonzero infinitely divisible differential; finite coefficient-compositum argument checked.

statement: In characteristic p and positive dimension, discrete formal smoothness holds exactly when K/k is separable and K has finite absolute p-rank
notes: Both necessities and a finite p-monomial presentation with canonical p-power lifts are proved. Independent algebra audit passed.

statement: A finite relative p-basis alone does not suffice over an arbitrary imperfect base
notes: Take k=K=Fp(s1,s2,...); the relative p-basis is empty but absolute p-rank is infinite. Under a perfect base the finite relative criterion is valid.

statement: An explicit one-dimensional noetherian domain has infinitely many cuspidal maximal local rings and only its generic point regular
notes: Finite-character localization of infinitely many cusps. Fresh-variable ideal argument proves the exact spectrum and noetherianity.

statement: The formally smooth fibre locus of a flat map of noetherian rings need not be open
notes: Fp to the infinite-cusp ring is flat; the locus is its nonopen generic point. Finite-presentation repair is SA23-A-13.

statement: The flat locus of a homomorphism between noetherian rings need not be open
notes: Frobenius on the same ring is flat only generically; an explicit cusp syzygy proves failure at every maximal ideal, including p=2.

statement: Finite presentation restores openness of the flat locus and of the formally smooth fibre locus for a flat morphism
notes: Opened Stacks Theorem37.15.1, Lemma10.137.16 and Lemma33.12.6; source hypotheses and pointwise fibre comparison verified.

statement: For a noetherian adically formally smooth map, the cotangent complex on every adic quotient is a projective module in degree zero
notes: Projectivity follows by continuous derivation lifting; completed local regularity and residue-field detection eliminate higher cotangent homology.

statement: Cotangent Ext groups of positive degree vanish for finite complete coefficients over a noetherian adically formally smooth algebra
notes: Derived inverse limit of Hom from projective quotient differentials; transition maps are surjective.

statement: Every noetherian adically complete formally smooth algebra lifts over a square-zero thickening, uniquely up to reduction-preserving isomorphism, with both forms of formal projectivity preserved
notes: AQ obstruction and ambiguity groups vanish; flatness, noetherianity, completeness and formal smoothness of the lift proved. Automorphisms are the stated derivations. Independent full audit passed.

statement: Opened complete-local and pseudo-finite-type lifting results are special cases and do not by themselves cover the general adic question
notes: EGA0IV19.7.2 and19.7.3; Perez Rodriguez2008 Definition1.3 and Corollary4.3. Exact hypotheses compared.

statement: Topological formal projectivity lifts through a noetherian square-zero flat deformation
notes: Continuous Hom represented by a filtered colimit of Ext; low-degree change of rings and Artin–Rees make the Tor obstruction pro-zero.

statement: Strict formal projectivity with a basis of projective quotients also lifts through that deformation
notes: Split quotient tower, arbitrary-rank idempotent lifting, complete product reconstruction, nilpotent Nakayama and explicit inverse continuity. Initial V0=B0 fixes tail indexing.
